title: Judging and comparing
intro: Adjectives and adverbs for saying how good, how bad and how much. Remember the four irregular comparatives that refuse más: mejor, peor, mayor, menor (see the opening section).

entries.note: Both shorten before a masculine singular noun: un buen día, un mal año.

ex.es: Fue un mal día para todos.
ex.en: It was a bad day for everyone.

entries.note: Never más bueno or más malo in comparisons. With the article they become the superlative: el mejor.
mi hermano mayor is my older brother. Also used of quantities: la mayor parte, most of.

ex.es: Mi hermana mayor vive en Chile.
ex.en: My older sister lives in Chile.

ex.es: Es tres años menor que yo.
ex.en: He's three years younger than me.

entries.note: me da igual means I don't mind. al igual que means just like.
diferente also works for different. parecerse a is to look like.

ex.es: Es distinto de lo que esperaba.
ex.en: It's different from what I expected.

entries.note: lo importante is the important thing — see lo in the opening section.
Both are invariable for gender: un examen difícil, una pregunta difícil.

ex.es: El examen fue más difícil de lo normal.
ex.en: The exam was harder than usual.

entries.note: lo antes posible means as soon as possible.

ex.en: It's impossible to get there on time.

entries.note: es cierto means it's true. Before a noun it means a certain: cierta persona.
See unit 5 for claro meaning of course.
bastante does the same job in speech — see unit 35.
sobre todo and principalmente are the adverbs.
en general means generally, on the whole.

entries.warn: muy goes before adjectives and adverbs, mucho with verbs and nouns. muy bien but me gusta mucho. Never muy mucho.

entries.note: Same split as muy and mucho. tan ... como is as ... as; tanto como as much as.

ex.es: No es tan difícil como parece.
ex.en: It isn't as hard as it looks.

entries.note: quizás with an s is equally correct. Both often take the subjunctive: quizá venga.
claro que sí and desde luego do the same job.
estar de acuerdo con is to agree with. On its own, de acuerdo means OK.
From valer — see unit 40. vale la pena intentarlo, it's worth trying.

ex.es: El viaje es largo pero vale la pena.
ex.en: The journey is long but it's worth it.
